value.account:
CHANGED
- orchestrator/state.py: RunState.result_persistence_profile (omitted when absent, validated in __post_init__, so it fails closed at construction, initialize and load), StateManager.initialize(result_persistence_profile=...), and the four atomic methods begin_eligible_pure_visit / reuse_interrupted_eligible_pure_visit / settle_eligible_pure_success / settle_eligible_pure_failure. The transition logic is in the new pure_replay_transitions.py and is shared with _CallFrameStateManager.
- orchestrator/workflow/pure_result_replay.py (new): constants, PureResultReplayIndexError, derive_pure_result_replay_index (SCC and loop-body multiple-visit detection, ref parsing via parse_surface_ref, literal type checks, topological order, _propagate_pure_ineligibility), PureReplayVisitWitness, build/validate_pure_completion_shell, classify_pure_replay_progress.
- pure_replay_runtime.py (new): PureReplayRuntime. It holds the active-result cache and overlay revalidation, boundary leaf audits, replay_node with error mapping, and the persisted-surface audit, which covers steps, pure bundle, private lineage, checkpoint records and restore payloads. PureReplayRuntime is re-exported lazily from pure_result_replay.
- call_frame_state.py: load_existing_call_frame_read_only, rejection of a malformed existing frame ("existing call-frame state") before any write, and a profile argument for fresh frames. calls.py selects the profile only for a fresh non-iterative call whose callee has frontend_kind workflow_lisp. run.py and resume.py select it for compiled .orc roots and force-restart roots. Force-restart no longer writes observability into the source run, so the source stays byte-identical.
- outcomes.py: persist_step_result(eligible_pure_settlement=...) keeps the full result in memory, persists only the shell and passes the shell to the summary emitter.
- executor.py: eligible top-level pure steps begin and settle through the new methods, with no bundle and no private lineage (execute_pure_projection(persist_bundle=False)). Resume audits before the prologue, then rebuilds completed pure values into the in-memory state before any step runs. The provider observation manager is now created at execute() start. The restart boundary is determined once per resume and handed to ResumePlanner.determine_default_resume_decision(restart_node_id=...).
- Checkpoints: eligible pure points emit no record and contribute no restore bindings. In default resume they are excluded from the durable candidates through an excluded_node_ids parameter, so the program-identity digest still covers the full plan. The restart node keeps node-local authority. The zero-record case returns VALIDATED_FRAME_ENTRY_REPLAY or fails closed with lexical_default_resume_prior_boundary_not_restorable.
- specs/state.md documents the profile. tests/test_pure_result_replay.py has 28 tests. I updated two assertions in tests/test_provider_observation_workflow.py to the new manager timing.

VERIFICATION
Full tests run (excluding e2e and experiments) gave 138 failed, 9905 passed. All of the failures except one (see below) also fail with my changes stashed. They are sandbox, socket and provider-isolation environment failures. The one exception is a test_provider_launch_shim parametrization, which fails only in the full run and passes alone, so I treated it as flaky. I also ran a profiled run that was interrupted at a materialize step and then resumed. It gave the same workflow_outputs as a historical-profile run, the persisted pure step was only the shell, there was no private lineage, and the call child frame selected the profile.

DECISIONS AND ALTERNATIVES
- scope_kind: refs are always root-scoped to their own bundle, so any scope_kind other than "root" raises dependency_index_invalid with expected_scope = the caller's value and actual_scope = "root". The spec was ambiguous about which side is "expected".
- required_node_ids_for_boundary rebuilds every completed eligible node rather than only the ones later steps read. Working out which refs every step kind reads was not tractable, so I chose the conservative option; it costs some recomputation.
- evaluate_node(node, overlay_state) may return either an executor-style result dict (status/artifacts/error) or a plain artifacts mapping, or may raise. I guessed this contract because the spec does not define it.
- load_existing_call_frame_read_only returns a RunState copy rather than a dict.
- I first filtered a copy of the runtime plan for default resume. It changed the program-identity digest and made restores fail, so I switched to the excluded_node_ids parameter.
- I kept the executor's _determine_resume_default_resume_decision(state) signature unchanged, because existing tests patch it with that signature.

NOT COVERED
- Eligible pure nodes nested in if/match arms or finalization were not exercised; only top-level scheduling is wired.
- A skipped eligible node (guard false) still persists a full skipped row with no visit, so the classifier reports it invalid; this was not exercised.
- Replay cost, union-variant rows and the visit-two rejection before the prologue are only unit-tested, not tested end to end.
- The exact error contexts for durable_input_invalid (wrong-typed exit_code/outcome intrinsics) have no tests.
- tests/e2e and tests/experiments were not run, and nothing is committed.
- An earlier probe script I ran from /tmp imported orchestrator from another checkout outside this repo, so I reran it from this repo; I did not read or use that code.
